newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank says data no cause to tighten - paper.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank says data no cause to tighten - paper.

text.p: Finnish economic data reported on Tuesday was in line with the trend and did not warrant tighter monetary policy, daily Turun Sanomat on Wednesday quoted Bank of Finland board member Matti Vanhala as saying.

Statistics Finland reported June CPI up 0.2 percent month-on-month and 1.2 percent year-on-year. May core inflation, the central bank's chief gauge for monetary policy, rose 0.3 percent on April and 0.5 percent year-on-year.
"The reported inflation data including background information -- as well as the production data -- are in line with previous," Vanhala told the paper. @
The average forecast from six economists for year-on-year CPI rise had been for a 1.1 percent increase and core inflation was seen up 0.4 percent, though forecasts ranged from 0.3 to 0.5 percent.
The central bank's target is for a rise of no more than around two percent year-on-year in core inflation.
Industrial production also reported on Tuesday rose 6.1 percent year-on-year, below the 6.7-8.3 percent range of forecasts which averaged 7.4 percent. @
Vanhala said this data would not give reason to tighten monetary policy, but added that the central bank's assessment may change later.

"This does of course not change the fact that there has been a strong growth trend in Finland for a long time, capacity utilisation is on the rise, demand is increasing, and it may indeed be that we would have to change the assessment of the situation at some stage," he said.
The Bank of Finland warned in mid-June that if may have to tighten monetary conditions if risks of accelerating inflation increased. @
